unit: workload points per newly assigned lead
business_reasoning: A newly assigned lead that has not yet been contacted weighs exactly one workload point in the reviewed capacity design (CAP-01). The ledger adds this amount to the selected RM for every operational recommendation it makes.

An operational recommendation is permitted only while the simulated post-assignment utilization stays strictly below the declared hard limit, the same strict test REL-13 applies before the assignment. An ordinary assignment must never push an RM to or past the limit (CAP-06), so a candidate whose workload would land exactly on it is skipped.

The ledger starts from the latest valid capacity snapshot at or before each decision. When a newer observed snapshot becomes effective for an RM, that snapshot replaces the ledger basis and the simulated additions accumulated against the older basis are reset to zero, because the observed snapshot already reflects the work the RM is actually carrying.

value: as_of_timestamp asc; priority_tier asc (P1,P2,P3); priority_score desc; sla_pressure desc; decision_id asc
business_reasoning: Decisions are processed in a single declared order so the ledger is deterministic and reproducible. Timestamp first because capacity is consumed in time order; priority tier and score next so that, at an identical instant, the more urgent lead claims capacity first; the decision identifier last as a stable final tie-break.
When every eligible candidate would exceed the hard limit after the assignment, the lead is held in the declared capacity queue rather than assigned beyond capacity.
